headline: Chicago leads
*six months running*
slides.fig_caption: Chicago's annual price gain in September, *No. 1* of the 20 major metros tracked
slides.sub: Nationally, prices rose just 2.1% from a year ago.

slides.title: Where prices *rose most*
slides.note: Miami climbed into the *top three* after two months in fourth place.

slides.label: of 19 reported metros saw *prices fall* from a year ago
slides.body: Seattle dropped 1.9%, the biggest decline for the fourth month in a row. Denver, Dallas, Las Vegas and Tampa also slipped.

slides.label: September inflation, *outpacing* the 2.1% national price gain
slides.body: After inflation, U.S. home prices have now fallen for 16 straight months. Before seasonal adjustment, the national index slipped 0.3% from August.

slides.title: Lead with *local numbers*
slides.body: National prices are barely rising, but metros are moving in very different directions. Chicago sellers are still seeing solid gains. Bring your market's own data to every pricing conversation.
